summary.text: Andrew Beeler is the Republican candidate for Michigan State Senate District 25 in the November 3, 2026 general election, having advanced from the August 4 Republican primary.
A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy veteran, he served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 2021 to 2025 and is now a small business owner in Port Huron.

paragraphs.text: Beeler was born in Port Huron, graduated from Cardinal Mooney Catholic High School, and served in the U.S. Navy from 2010 to 2019.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Naval Academy in 2014.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was a surface warfare officer who deployed to the Western Pacific and the Arabian Gulf before leaving active duty in May 2019.
Beeler won election to the Michigan House of Representatives in 2020, defeating Stephanie Armstrong-Helton in District 83 with 65.5% of the vote.
He was re-elected in 2022 in District 64, first defeating incumbent Gary Eisen in the Republican primary and then Charles Howell in the general election.
His committee assignments in 2021-2022 included the Education, Health Policy, Military, Veterans and Homeland Security (as majority vice-chair) and Tax Policy committees.
In his survey, Beeler said he served as Republican caucus vice chair, as assistant Republican leader, and as chair of the House Republican Campaign Committee.
He said he did not seek re-election to the House, bought a small business in Port Huron, and announced his Senate campaign in November 2025.
Beeler listed his key messages as "Families First," protecting farmers, and supporting small business.
He named public safety, tax reform, agriculture policy and constitutional rights as the policy areas he is most passionate about.
